newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's opposition seeks budget nullification.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's opposition seeks budget nullification.

text.p: A Kenyan high court on Friday started hearing a petition by the opposition seeking to nullify the country's 1997/98 budget on grounds that it was not read audibly.

Opposition lawyer, Muturi Kigano, urged the court to nullify the budget which was delivered last week by Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi under chaotic conditions as opposition members of parliament tried to disrupt the speech to press demands for constitutional reforms.
President Daniel arap Moi, who must call presidential and parliamentary elections later this year, has ruled out constitutional reforms in this east African nation before the polls.
Earlier this week Moi censured the opposition for taking the budget wrangle to court, saying parliament was the country's supreme legal body and as such could not be overruled by a court.
"We ask the court to exert its authority and express its displeasure and censure the president through a proper ruling," Kigano said.
Government lawyer George Oraro urged the court to dismiss the case on grounds that the speaker of parliament was immune from prosecution and could not therefore be petitioned in a court of law.
"The constitution clearly states that the speaker is immune (from prosecution). To allow this case to continue would be the beginning of the killing of the legislature in this country," said Oraro.
The opposition challenged the legality of the budget in the courts on the grounds that Mudavadi failed to read it audibly and that Speaker Francis ole Kaparo failed to ensure quiet in the chamber.
High court Judge Moijo ole Keiwua is expected to make a ruling later on Friday.
Legal experts give the case little chance of success. But in the unlikely event of the opposition succeeding, then the president would be compelled under Kenyan law to dissolve parliament.
On Thursday, Kenya's National Assembly passed the budget, side-stepping an opposition boycott and the legal challenge.

The budget was approved on Thursday evening with only members of parliament from the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) and one opposition MP in the chamber, the Daily Nation and East African Standard said.
Opposition MPs have boycotted budget debates after disrupting Mudavadi's budget speech on June 19 to back demands for sweeping constitutional reforms before elections due this year.

In another pro-reform move Kenneth Matiba, chairman of the opposition FORD-Asili party, said he would not register as a voter and called on his supporters to boycott the elections, newspapers and an aide to Matiba said.

"Matiba has said that unless some constitutional reforms are put in place he will not register as a voter because rigging has already started through the registration of voters," the aide, declining to be quoted by name, told Reuters by telephone.

"Most of the opposition has said no elections without reforms and Matiba has just taken the lead. His supporters should boycott the election," the aide said. He added Matiba was abroad in London and would return late next week.
Matiba came second to Moi in Kenya's landmark multi-party elections in 1992 which the opposition says were unfair because of the pro-government constitution and electoral rules.
Matiba is the first prominent opposition leader to publicly back a boycott of this year's polls, whose dates have not been announced by Moi.
